A platform in seven days, and what the eighth day taught me

Uplink IT Academy went from an idea to seven working rooms in about a week. The eighth day was about what to remove.

I wanted a place where studying for a certification feels like the first week of a job. So every exam question became a ticket, every lab became a device you can break, and the help desk became a queue with tools.

The method was simple: build the room, fill it with real content, then break it on a phone. If it survived the phone, it stayed. If it did not, it went back to the bench.

What the eighth day taught me is that the content pipeline matters more than the interface. A lab that cannot grade itself is a lab that will one day fail a paying learner. So every lab now replays its own solution before it is allowed to go live, and a builder adds one new lab per track every morning while I sleep.

The platform is at academy.lemonshops.app. The free samples are in every room.
